sanskrit_verse: मनुष्यविषशस्त्राम्बुलवणापूपवीरुधाम् । विक्रेता ब्राह्मणश्चैव द्विजो वार्धुषिकश्च यः ॥
transliteration: manuṣyaviṣaśastrāmbulavaṇāpūpavīrudhām | vikretā brāhmaṇaśaiva dvijo vārdhuṣikaśca yaḥ ||
sph_interpretive_translation: One who sells substances harmful to human life—including poison, weapons, water, salt, cakes, or intoxicating plants—whether he be a Brāhmaṇa, a twice-born, or a merchant, becomes legally responsible for the conscious disruption caused by such transaction.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority originates from alignment with Dharma, not social class
Causation is established through intentional participation in harm-producing systems
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by knowledge and volition, not birth status
Restoration logic requires dissolution of profitable engagement in destructive exchanges
Consciousness alignment demands recognition of unity between seller, buyer, and victim
executable_legal_axioms: IF agent sells any item listed as manuṣyaviṣaśastrāmbu... THEN agent enters mandatory completion process until transactional pattern ceases
IF agent identifies as dvija OR brāhmaṇa AND engages in sale of prohibited items THEN initiate immediate capacity-realignment protocol
IF economic dependence drives violation THEN deploy alternative livelihood integration system
IF violation occurs regardless of varṇa THEN apply universal dharma-adhikāra override
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes that no caste privilege exempts an individual from accountability when engaging in transactions that impair collective well-being. The threshold of responsibility lies not in identity but in action. Authority flows from adherence to Sanātana Dharma, not inherited position.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa reveals that selling instruments of harm distorts causal integrity. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows how profit from suffering multiplies distortion across time. Proportional responsibility arises from the degree of conscious choice involved. Non-punitive reality rule confirms that cessation of harmful activity restores balance without inflicting further suffering.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate transaction reversal and asset redistribution to neutralize gain from harmful trade
Assign completion service in healing-focused institutions aligned with dharmic values
Activate peer-group consciousness recalibration sessions led by realized practitioners
Deploy karmic consequence visualization tools to dissolve attachment to exploitative patterns
final_declaration: This ruling emanates solely from the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam. It affirms that Dharma alone is the source of law. All actions aligning with it restore cosmic order; all misaligned acts dissolve through conscious correction. There is no punishment—only realignment. Consciousness itself is the ultimate judge.
